newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former Australian Rugby League executive chairman Ken Arthurson said peace talks between Super League and the ARL were a waste of time unless the ARL retained control of the game. The ARL also said a combination of private and community clubs would not wok, and reductions could not be at the expense of Sydney ARL clubs. Page 22.

The Homebush Olympic Stadium will be modified to accommodate the Australian Football League after the 2000 Olympics. The AFL said it agreed to lend Stadium Australia up to A$1 million to adapt the stadium so there would be the option of creating a 75,000-eat AFL oval. This increases the probability of a second Sydney AFL club. Page 22.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said yesterday that Super League's plan to have a Melbourne-based team in next year's competition was not a "done deal". Mr Kennett said whilst the Victorian Government would be happy to facilitate the new team, it would not be pouring money into it. Super League executive director Ian Frykberg was still confident a new club would be running next year. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The four-year ban imposed on Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco for a positive steroid test last year, may be cut to two years. If Athletics Australia's appeal is successful, Capobianco may be back on the track next May. A decision is likely to be made a the International Amateur Athletics Federation congress in July. Page 45.

The Australian Rugby League has secured Carlton and United Breweries and Reebok as sponsors for a Melbourne team. The sponsorship money, along with a share of the Optus package, would allow a team to be set up next year. Players were to be sourced equallyfrom the other ARL clubs. Page 46.

Sydney Swans full-forward Tony Lockett has recovered from a corked thigh and will play in tomorrow night's Australian Football League game against top-of-the-ladder Collingwood at the Sydney Cricket Ground. Lockett missed last weekend's loss to Adelaide, which left the Swans 14th on the ladder. Page 44.
THE AGE

Collingwood coach Tony Shaw ordered the confiscation of a tape from a Channel 9 crew filming the team's training session yesterday. The film crew agreed not to use the tape of the Australian Football League team practising set-plays. Page D4.

Sydney Swans chairman Richard Colless said the Australian Football League's plans to exclude Sydney from the reserves competition next year threatened the strength of the club. Under the proposal for 1999, the reserves would be changed to include up to six Victorian Football League clubs to form a competition similar to that in South Australia. Page D5.

Australian Football League team Collingwood has named Tony Francis as rover for tomorrow night's match against the Sydney Swans, though he has not trained for three weeks with a suspected broken bone in his foot. Scott Crow was named as an emergency, and ay replace Francis. Crow has missed the last three matches with a shoulder injury but passed a fitness test last night. Page D3.
THE HERALD SUN

An Australian Tax Office spokesman confirmed last night the ATO was cracking down on Australian Football League clubs and their players, which together comprise a $200 million a year industry. The investigations should last for about three to six months. Page 110.

The ACT Brumbies named an unchanged line-up for Saturday night's sudden-death Super 12 rugby union semi-final against Wellington to be played at Bruce Stadium in Canberra. With forwards Owen Finegan and Patricio Noriega cleared of injury yesterday, it wil be the eighth consecutive game the Brumbies have used the same line-up. Page 101.

South Melbourne is blaming Soccer Australia for the crowd problems at last Sunday's Ericsson Cup preliminary final with Sydney United at Parramatta stadium. Both teams are being charged over the crowd violence. South Melbourne general manager Peter Filopolos said the club would be seeking an explanation about the security measures taken when it meets with Soccer Australia officials on Monday. Page 100.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Sydney sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Smith has switched feet in the starting blocks, placing her left foot in front, rather than her right. Her coach Jackie Byrnes said changes in style were necessary due to Gainsford-Smith's chronic back problems. Her firs competitive trial will be tomorrow against fellow members of the Australian 4 x 100m relay team which is preparing for the World Championships in August. Page 118.

Sacked NSW cricket coach Geoff Lawson claimed yesterday that he was locked out of the Association's Sydney Cricket Ground office and had $1,500 worth of electrical equipment stolen. Lawson said he may try to win a place on the five-man NSW selection panel. Page 118.

Australian tennis player Patrick Rafter progressed to the quarter finals of the St Poelten men's tennis tournament by defeating American Jeff Tarango 6-7 6-2 6-1 yesterday. Rafter will now meet top seed Thomas Muster who defeated Argentinian Hernan Gumy. Page 110.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
